claim: Main stress is assigned within the prosodic word with suffixes typically extraprosodic; long vowels are always stressed, and secondary stress alternates to the left of main stress.

prosody: secondary stress alternates before main stress
source_forms.weight: closed syllables pattern with monomoraic open syllables; consonants are non-moraic in the analysis

normalized_environment: stress conditioned by moraic vowel quantity and morphological constituency
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The analysis explicitly treats suffixes as typically, not invariably, extraprosodic; no stronger categorical suffix claim is inferred.

claim: Before a simple onset, vowel-final morphemes do not undergo the consonant-vowel metathesis characteristic of consonant-final forms; their final vowel may instead surface as secondary articulation or delete.

repairs: high vowel -> secondary articulation in appropriate contexts

formal_environment: V-final morpheme + C V inside phonological phrase
normalized_environment: V-final + simple onset: no VC-metathesis; V realization conditioned by quality/context
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Metathesis occurs in other structural environments, especially C-final forms before CC/CVV; this record is not a general anti-metathesis statement.

claim: Before a vowel-initial following morpheme, a final consonant of the first morpheme resyllabifies as the onset of the following syllable.

source_forms.generalization: final C becomes onset before following V

exceptions_or_counterexamples: If additional vowel sequences would violate other restrictions, secondary articulation, metathesis, or deletion can also apply; onset resyllabification is one component of the repair system.

claim: An unstressed prevocalic high vowel can be realized as secondary articulation on an adjacent consonant; the pattern occurs both morpheme-internally and across morpheme boundaries.
formal_environment: V[+high,-stress] / C __ V or __ C V depending restructuring
normalized_environment: unstressed high V -> glide/secondary articulation adjacent to prevocalic C
scope: within words and across relevant morpheme boundaries
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Vowel deletion is used when vowel-preserving strategies fail; high-high sequences have separate restrictions.
section: 2.2 Avoidance of onsetless syllables / hiatus repair

claim: Vowel deletion is a last-resort repair in the analysis: vowel-preserving strategies such as metathesis or secondary articulation are preferred where they can satisfy the relevant syllable constraints.

source_forms.repair_preference: metathesis / secondary articulation > vowel deletion where structurally viable

normalized_environment: repair selection minimizes deletion while satisfying ONSET/complex-margin restrictions
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Deletion does surface when competing vowel-preserving repairs fail, so it is not absent from the language.

claim: For vowel-final forms before a CVV-initial morpheme, metathesis would create an onsetless syllable, so high-vowel glide/secondary-articulation formation can surface instead.

source_forms.repair: high V -> glide/secondary articulation rather than metathesis

normalized_environment: avoid onsetless syllable after concatenation; choose glide formation over metathesis
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The outcome depends on vowel quality and the availability of a suitable adjacent consonant; it is not generalized to all V+CVV sequences without qualification.

claim: When the final vowel of a VVC morpheme is transposed or deleted in the relevant phrase-medial repairs, the preceding vowel lengthens.
formal_environment: V V C]morph under final-V transposition/deletion
normalized_environment: V1 V2 C -> V1: ... when V2 is displaced/deleted by repair
scope: VVC-final morphemes undergoing the specified repairs
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The statement is tied to the repair environment; it is not staged as a general rule that all vowel loss causes compensatory lengthening.

claim: Phrase-initial consonant clusters that satisfy the paper's Sonority Principle can surface intact; Leti does not generally repair every initial cluster by epenthesis or deletion.
normalized_environment: surface #CC licensed if sonority profile is acceptable
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Clusters that violate the Sonority Principle behave differently; the source therefore supports a sonority-conditioned restriction rather than a blanket permission for #CC.
